summary_for_children: Al-Hijr says Allah protects the Quran, shows the stars, mountains and winds as signs, and tells of the people of al-Hijr who carved homes in the mountains.

unique_world.visual_theme: A sandstone valley ringed by cliffs with five carved doorways, two rocks, a well, palms and a tent, and a map table

primary_mechanic.text: Take a rubbing of each carved doorway by keeping still, then fit every rubbing onto a map of the valley where its doorway stands, using the landmarks and memory (15:80-84).

unique_world.narrative_structure: Measure stone, then exploring the cliffs for rubbings, then the map table, then the road sign
world_assets: five carved rock fronts with doorways and distinct patterns
map table and a paper map with landmarks
environment_behaviour: the paper whitens as the rubbing comes through and smudges if you move
placed rubbings show on the map
unique_world.learning_objective: Look closely at signs left in the land, and remember what truly keeps us safe (15:75-84)

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The City Carved in Stone
story_library.children_narration: Some ancient communities built impressive homes in mountains and rocky landscapes. Their buildings were strong, but their strength did not mean they could ignore Allah's guidance. Surah Al-Hijr reminds us about the creation of Adam, Iblis's arrogance, the visitors who came to Ibrahim, the people of Lut, and the people of Al-Hijr who rejected the signs they were given. The surah teaches that pride can lead people away from truth, while remembering Allah's mercy and guidance can lead them back.

world_idea.title: The Carved Mountains
world_idea.description: Children explore rock-carved passages, examine historical-style building techniques, and uncover narrated story stations connected to the surah.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
story_library.rule_conflicts_resolved: The creation of Adam and Iblis (15:26-44) concerns the unseen: reading only, nothing pictured.
